items.followUp: State one advantage of wind energy and one advantage of geothermal energy.

rubric.why: Identifies wind energy and explains its source or use.
rubric.description: Wind energy comes from moving air and can be used to generate electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying moving or blowing air as the source and 1 mark for explaining its use, such as driving turbines to generate electricity.

rubric.why: Identifies geothermal energy and explains its source or use.
rubric.description: Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth, which can be used for heating or electricity generation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heat inside the Earth as the source and 1 mark for giving a use, such as heating or generating electricity.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is obtained from moving air and can be used to turn turbines to generate electricity.
Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth; it can be used for heating or to generate electricity.

items.followUp: A force of 100 N acts at 60° to the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Uses the correct component relations for an angle measured from the horizontal road.
rubric.description: Horizontal component is F cos θ and vertical component is F sin θ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct component formulae.

rubric.why: The horizontal component is calculated from the force and angle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for the correct value with unit.

rubric.why: The vertical component is calculated from the force and angle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for the correct value with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, θ = 30° to the horizontal road.
Horizontal component: Fₓ = F cos θ.
Vertical component: Fᵧ = F sin θ.
The horizontal component is 173.2 N and the vertical component is 100 N.

items.followUp: What is a thermometer? Briefly describe how a clinical thermometer works.

rubric.why: Gives the purpose of a thermometer.
rubric.description: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an instrument and 1 mark for stating that it measures temperature.

rubric.why: Explains the construction or working principle of a liquid-in-glass thermometer.
rubric.description: The thermometer contains liquid in a bulb connected to a narrow capillary; the liquid expands when heated and contracts when cooled, and its level is read on a scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the bulb and narrow capillary or the liquid column, and 1 mark for explaining expansion/contraction with temperature or reading the liquid level on a scale.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
A liquid-in-glass thermometer has a bulb containing liquid connected to a narrow glass capillary tube.
When the temperature rises, the liquid expands and moves up the capillary; when it falls, the liquid contracts and moves down.
The temperature is read from the liquid level against the scale marked on the thermometer.

items.followUp: Estimate the number of seconds in 12 years.

rubric.why: Uses a reasonable estimate by converting years into seconds.
rubric.description: Set-up: 15 years × 365 days/year × 24 hours/day × 60 minutes/hour × 60 seconds/minute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid conversion set-up or equivalent calculation.

rubric.why: Gives a reasonable estimated age in seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct estimate with seconds as the unit.

modelAnswer: Given: age = 15 years; take 1 year ≈ 365 days.
Time in seconds = 15 × 365 × 24 × 60 × 60 s.
Time in seconds = 473,040,000 s ≈ 4.7 × 10⁸ s.

items.followUp: Explain how to use a stopwatch to measure the time taken for a ball to roll down a ramp.

rubric.why: Describes starting the stopwatch at the beginning of the measured interval.
rubric.description: Reset the stopwatch to zero and start it when the event begins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly starting the stopwatch at the beginning of the interval; resetting to zero may also be mentioned.

rubric.why: Describes stopping and reading the elapsed time.
rubric.description: Stop the stopwatch when the event ends and read the elapsed time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stopping at the end of the interval and reading the time.

modelAnswer: Reset the stopwatch to zero and start it when the event begins.
Stop it when the event ends and read the elapsed time shown.

items.followUp: Express 3,000 g and 64 × 10⁻⁸ g using suitable prefixes.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct prefix form.

rubric.why: Converts the small mass to a suitable SI prefix correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct prefix form.

items.followUp: Define displacement and state whether it is a vector or scalar quantity.

rubric.why: Defines position in relation to a reference point.
rubric.description: Position tells the location of an object relative to a reference point or origin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining position as the location of an object with reference to a point or origin.

rubric.why: Correctly classifies position as a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that position is a vector.

modelAnswer: Position is the location of an object relative to a reference point or origin.
Position is a vector quantity.

items.followUp: Define average speed and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines speed as distance travelled per unit time.
rubric.description: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating distance travelled to time taken.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of speed.
rubric.description: The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time.
Its SI unit is metre per second (m/s).
